newsitem.title: UK: Wheat above $4 threshold, tin at 19-month-low.
newsitem.headline: Wheat above $4 threshold, tin at 19-month-low.

text.p: Wheat futures stayed above the psychological threshold of $4 per bushel in Chicago on Monday on weather concerns and rumours Russia may have been offered credit to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of wheat.
Elsewhere, tin on the London Metal Exchange (LME) fell to the lowest level in 19 months at one stage but in other metals and softs markets, activity was dull given seasonal year-end factors.
By 1733 GMT, the December wheat futures were 3.00 cents up at $409 cents a bushel. Traders said the gains followed concerns that cold weather in some winter wheat areas could damage part of the crop.
Rumours Russia might have been offered wheat credit was supportive but gains were limited by talk a Russian delegates' trip to Washington has been cancelled.
Russia is a major grains importer.

Last week, wheat prices were boosted by buying news from India and Iraq. Traders said a key factor was that India, home of the "Green Revolution" in Third World agriculture, turned from wheat seller to importer.
In base metals, tin on the LME ended the afternoon kerb just off the fresh 19-month-low of $5,680 a tonne on fund liquidation.
Nickel closed kerb weaker after a fresh 26-month nadir, weighed by weak technical picture, a stock build-up on Friday and threat of exports from Russia.
Precious metal prices drifted within narrow price bands, with gold was finding some support around $368 an ounce but showed little enthusiasm for breaking out of a tight range.
